title: Yet the New World may long have been partly known; Besoldus; Japheth origin; Fuller and others
pass_a_gloss: Compare Nicholas Fuller, Theological Miscellanies book 1, chapter 4; Vandermylius On the Belgian Language chapter 25; Acosta book 1, chapter 24; Claude Duret, History of Languages chapter 78; Peter Bertius in his contracted maps belonging toward America; Johannes Goropius Becanus in the Antwerp Origins, in the Niloscopium; Lipsius, Stoic Physiology book 2, dissertation 19. And the inhabitants stand as believed to have been of Cymbric or ancient Teutonic and Scythian origin from Japheth the son belonging toward Noah (Genesis 9:19, 27). Yet it stands as more likely that the islands, and the adjacent continent belonging toward that New World, stood as also long ago, many ages before, not wholly unknown toward our world, as the polyhistor Christopher Besoldus, professor belonging toward Tubingen, demonstrates at length in his Political Discourses on the growth belonging toward empire, chapter 4, year 10.
pass_b_english: Yet it is more likely that the islands, and the adjacent continent of that New World, were also long ago, many ages before, not wholly unknown to our world, as the polyhistor Christopher Besoldus, professor of Tubingen, demonstrates at length in his Political Discourses on the growth of empire, chapter 4, year 10; and the inhabitants are believed to have been of Cymbric or ancient Teutonic and Scythian origin from Japheth the son of Noah (Genesis 9:19, 27). Compare Nicholas Fuller, Theological Miscellanies book 1, chapter 4; Vandermylius On the Belgian Language chapter 25; Acosta book 1, chapter 24; Claude Duret, History of Languages chapter 78; Peter Bertius in his contracted maps of America; Johannes Goropius Becanus in the Antwerp Origins, in the Niloscopium; Lipsius, Stoic Physiology book 2, dissertation 19.
source_text: Vero tamen similius sit, insulas, adjacentemque novi illius orbis continentem, olim quoque multa ante saecula orbi nostro non plane incognitam fuisse, ut late demonstrat polyhistor, Christophorus Besoldus prof. Tubingensis discurs. polit. de incrementis imper. cap. 4. an. 10. & Cymbricae seu priscae Teutonicae Scythicaeque originis fuisse creduntur incolae ex Japheto Nochi filio, Gen. 9.v.19.27. Confer Nicolaum Fullerum Miscell. Theol. lib. 1. cap. 4. Vandermylium de lingua Belgica cap. 25. Acostam lib. 1. cap. 24. Claude Duret Histoire de Langues cap. 78. Petrum Bertium in tabulis contractis de America, Joh. Goropium Becanum in Origin. Antuerp. in Niloscopio, Lipsium stoicae physiolog. lib. 2. diss. 19.
